source.title: Convergent Linear Representations of Emergent Misalignment
source.authors: Anna Soligo; Edward Turner; Senthooran Rajamanoharan; Neel Nanda

page_placements.theme: Geometric measures, task values and causal interpretation

record.file_problem: The full paper text, including appendices, is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies linear activation directions that mediate emergent misalignment, but does not test feature superposition, sparse-feature overlap, capacity competition, neuron polysemanticity, or SAE feature completeness.
record.gate_note: The paper reports interventions and measurements on misalignment directions. These are adjacent evidence about linear representations in LLMs, not tests of the claim versions: the study does not measure superposition or feature geometry under sparsity and capacity pressure. Accordingly, the direction results are recorded as fits_no_version findings.
record.test_reason: The study extracts difference-of-means misalignment directions in Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct EM fine-tunes and tests steering, ablation and transfer. It never measures superposition, feature sparsity or capacity, neuron polysemanticity, SAE features, or feature dimensionality. Superposition-adjacent work (Bricken et al.; Templeton et al.) is only cited as background for the linear representation hypothesis. Its remark that a multi-dimensional misalignment representation is not ruled out concerns a behavioural concept direction, not superposed features, so it does not test V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that EM fine-tunes converge on a similar linear misalignment direction that can induce misalignment and ablate it across fine-tunes. They caution that this does not preclude a more complex multi-dimensional representation. They also report that some LoRA adapters specialise for the medical context while others drive general misalignment.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses mean-difference activation directions, steering and ablation, plus LoRA scalar probes, rather than the toy-network feature-sparsity and geometry methods of the original source.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering efficacy varies by layer and steering scale; the authors report greater efficacy in central layers. Ablation effects differ between layer-wise, single-direction-across-layers, and layer-24-only conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: A single mean-diff direction induces EM when added to the chat model and removes most EM when ablated. This holds across three Qwen-14B fine-tunes, with transfer ablation cutting misalignment by 90% and 78%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent misalignment in Qwen2.5-14B fine-tunes is mediated by a shared linear direction that transfers across fine-tunes.

fits_no_version.finding: The rank-1 LoRA B vector and the mean-diff direction have cosine 0.04 at layer 24. Yet ablating the mean-diff direction removes nearly all EM, and their downstream activation effects converge to cosine 0.42.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nearly orthogonal directions at one layer can have converging downstream behavioural effects.

record.problems: The authors state that evidence comes from a small number of fine-tunes on one model. Evaluation uses eight questions and LLM judges; the paper notes judge reliability as a limitation. It does not investigate the superposition claim's central feature-sparsity and capacity conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No superposition-specific results were reported. Results on semantic-topic steering, scalar probing, LoRA steering, and scalar patching were omitted because they do not measure any claim version's feature geometry or superposition.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweeps or feature geometry.
All: no capacity or dedicated-dimension analysis.
All: no measure of feature spread across neurons and no SAE/dictionary recovery.
All: SAEs are not trained or evaluated.
All: dimensionality of superposed features is not tested. The multi-dimensional caveat concerns the misalignment concept direction only.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from discusses to cites_only: superposition is not discussed, and only related SAE and monosemanticity work is cited. All rows correctly link to none, and no verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature sparsity, overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Feature distribution across neurons and recovery of sparse features with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representation.
Whether the features involved in superposition are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
